body: With `compute_(being|end)_pass`, we can now properly determine the lifetime of compute encoders.
MTL::Event is a much simpler barrier synchronisation mechanism and allows us to work on all supported OSs. It also better aligns with how Godot generates synchronisation barriers.
This fixes a validation bug.
This wrapper class allows us to cache the gpu_address once, rather than call the Obj-C selector optionally, every time we access it.

This delays fetching the CA::MetalDrawable until the texture is actually needed, which prevents blocking on the main thread until it is absolutely necessary, which gives the window server more time to render the previous frames and release previous drawables.
only removing `final` as it's added at the class level
Presentation is more efficient and we don't need to use completion handlers.
This is really helpful when debugging.
Helps drivers like Metal, which don't need layout transitions.

Hmm, is a spin lock a good idea here? I feel like `_pool_allocate` has the potential to take a while to execute so the lock may end up burning a lot of cycles in heavily contended scenarios. Does this happen in practice?
I figure releasing MTL::Heap objects can be costly, so I'd move this to outside the spin lock to not unnecessarily block other threads waiting on it.
Same here as above, move outside the spin lock so it doesn't unnecessarily block other threads waiting on it.

`SpinLock` is implemented using an [`os_unfair_lock`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/os/os_unfair_lock_lock), which is an efficient Darwin kernel lock:

> A low-level lock that allows waiters to block efficiently on contention.
That's a very misleading name then, haha. But alright, fair!
I'll move both of those outside the lock 👍🏻
